subject: hindi
book: Aroh Bhag 1 (आरोह भाग 1); Vitan Bhag 1 (वितान भाग 1)

concepts.text: Premchand (1880-1936), real name Dhanpat Rai, born at Lamhi near Varanasi; known as उपन्यास सम्राट
Major novels: सेवासदन, रंगभूमि, कर्मभूमि, गबन, गोदान; stories collected in मानसरोवर (8 parts)
Edited the journals हंस and जागरण; first wrote in Urdu as 'Nawab Rai'
His approach: आदर्शोन्मुख यथार्थवाद (realism that leans towards an ideal); focus on farmers, the poor and social evils
Setting: the British salt monopoly created a salt department where bribe-taking (ऊपरी आय) was common
Vanshidhar's old father advises him to choose a post for its extra income, not its rank
Father's image: monthly salary is the full moon (पूर्णमासी का चाँद) that soon shrinks; extra income is a flowing stream (बहता स्रोत)
Remark that daughters 'grow like weeds' shows the low status of girls and dowry worries
Vanshidhar becomes salt inspector (दारोगा) at the Yamuna crossing; the family rejoices
Night scene: carts of Pandit Alopideen of Datagunj carry illegal salt across the Yamuna bridge
Alopideen is sure that Lakshmi (money) can buy anyone, and offers a bribe
The bribe keeps rising (from one thousand up to forty thousand) but Vanshidhar refuses and orders his arrest
Clash of धर्म (duty) and धन (wealth) at the bridge: duty crushes wealth
Gossip spreads through the town the next morning: the world sleeps but its tongue stays awake
In court, lawyers and officials favour the rich; Alopideen is acquitted and Vanshidhar is rebuked
Vanshidhar loses his job; father, mother and wife scorn him and call his education wasted
Alopideen arrives at Vanshidhar's house in a chariot; the family fears more trouble
He offers Vanshidhar the post of permanent manager of all his estates with a good salary and perks
Vanshidhar, moved to tears, accepts; honesty is finally recognised even by the corrupt
Idealistic ending typical of Premchand; debate on whether accepting the post was right
वंशीधर: honest, dutiful, fearless, educated young man who values integrity over money
पंडित अलोपीदीन: rich, influential, clever, believes in the power of money, yet able to respect honesty
वृद्ध मुंशी (father): worldly and practical; supports corruption out of poverty and greed
Lawyers, officials and the crowd: a society that bows to wealth
Central theme: conflict between honesty (धर्म) and wealth (धन); honesty wins in the end
Satire on corruption in government service and the justice system (justice and policy as toys of wealth)
Question of the real value of education versus mere literacy
Social realism of colonial India: poverty, bribery, greed, status of women
Possible alternative titles and their justification (e.g. सत्य की जीत, ईमानदारी का फल)
Hindustani language mixing Hindi, Urdu and colloquial words (e.g. दारोगा, मुंशी, हुक्म, ऐतबार)
Rich use of idioms: फूले न समाना, हाथ मलना, सिर-माथे पर लेना, मुँह छिपाना, इज्जत धूल में मिलना
Irony and satire in the narration; vivid word-pictures (चित्रात्मकता)
Striking images: salary as moon, extra income as stream, reasoning that strengthens an illusion

sections.name: 1.8 प्रश्न-अभ्यास: पाठ के साथ / पाठ के आसपास / भाषा की बात (exercise types)

concepts.text: Character questions: whom you like most and why; two sides of Alopideen's personality
Explain given lines with context (सप्रसंग व्याख्या) and their hidden meaning
Opinion questions: was Vanshidhar right to accept the job; propose an alternative ending
Relate to today: which government posts people crave and why; how the rich escape the law
Personal experience: when education felt useless or meaningful; literacy vs education
Language tasks: find idioms, proverbs and Hindi-Urdu mixed words; adjectives for salary; use phrases in new contexts
Krishna Sobti (1925-2019), born in Gujrat (now in Pakistan); known for bold themes and earthy language
Works: ज़िंदगीनामा, मित्रो मरजानी, डार से बिछुड़ी, ऐ लड़की, सूरजमुखी अँधेरे के, दिलो-दानिश, हम हशमत
Awards: Sahitya Akademi (ज़िंदगीनामा) and Jnanpith (2017)
The lesson is from हम हशमत, a collection of शब्दचित्र (word portraits)
The author wanders through old Delhi near Jama Masjid/Matiyamahal and stops at a dark bakery
She meets Miyan Nasiruddin, a proud khandani nanbai (traditional bread-maker) who claims to bake 56 kinds of roti
Interview-style talk: he suspects the author is a newspaper reporter (अखबारनवीस)
He learnt the craft from his father Miyan Barkat Shahi and grandfather Miyan Kallan
Learning by doing: apprentices start by washing utensils and tending the bhatti before baking
Claim that his ancestors baked for the royal kitchen; the riddle of a bread 'baked without fire, made without water'
He becomes evasive and irritated when asked which king it was
Names of breads: बाकरखानी, शीरमाल, ताफ़तान, बेसनी, खमीरी, रूमाली, गाव-दीदा, गाज़ेबान, तुनकी
He talks about workers' wages and the falling respect for the craft
Expert craftsman proud of his family trade (खानदानी पेशा)
Boastful, witty and sometimes short-tempered; his mood changes quickly
Sees skill learnt through practice (तालीम) as true education
Pained that new generations do not value traditional work
Dignity of labour and pride in one's work
Handing down traditional skills from generation to generation
Decline of old crafts and the craftsman's place in a changing society
Why he is called the मसीहा (saviour) of nanbais
Genre: शब्दचित्र, an interview-style sketch with lively dialogue
Language mixes Hindi, Urdu and Punjabi with Delhi's spoken flavour
Humour and gentle irony in the author's questions
Key words: नानबाई, भट्टी, खानदानी, तालीम, अखबारनवीस, मोहल्ला, कारीगर

sections.name: 2.6 प्रश्न-अभ्यास: पाठ के साथ / पाठ के आसपास / भाषा की बात (exercise types)

concepts.text: Why the author was curious about Miyan Nasiruddin; why he took her for a reporter
Explain his views on learning a craft and on his ancestors
How his mood changed during the conversation, and why
Interview task: talk to a local craftsman and write a word-portrait
Language: find Urdu/Punjabi words, idioms and spoken-style sentences; rewrite them in standard Hindi

chapters.title: आरोह: सत्यजित राय — अपू के साथ ढाई साल

concepts.text: Satyajit Ray (1921-1992), Kolkata; world-famous film-maker, writer and illustrator
Films: पथेर पांचाली (1955), अपराजितो, अपुर संसार (Apu trilogy), चारुलता, शतरंज के खिलाड़ी, सद्गति, घरे बाइरे
Created the detective Feluda and Professor Shonku stories in Bangla
Honours: Bharat Ratna and an honorary Oscar (1992)
The lesson is a memoir (संस्मरण) translated from Bangla into Hindi (by Vilas Giri)
The film is based on Bibhutibhushan Bandyopadhyay's novel पथेर पांचाली
Shooting stretched over two and a half years for lack of money
Ray then worked in an advertising company and shot only when funds came in
Main location: the village of Boral near Kolkata
Search for a boy to play Apu: a newspaper ad failed; the boy was found on a neighbour's roof
Kaas-flower (काशफूल) field scene: half shot, then cattle ate the flowers; the crew waited a year
Train scene: several trains used; matching the smoke for continuity
The dog Bhulo died; a look-alike dog was found to finish the scene
The actor playing the sweet-seller (Shrinivas) died; a substitute was filmed from behind
Rain scene: no money in the rainy season; finally shot in autumn rain with the children shivering
The rented house in Boral and the 'mad' neighbour (Subodh-da) who suspected the crew
A snake in the house that villagers would not let be killed
The elderly actress Chunibala Devi as Indir Thakrun
Patience, determination and devotion to art despite hardship
Realistic film-making with real villages and non-professional actors
Importance of continuity (निरंतरता) in film shooting
Villagers' cooperation, and their suspicion of outsiders
Genre: संस्मरण; first-person narration with humour and honesty
Film terms: शूटिंग, सीन, शॉट, कैमरा, कंटिन्युइटी, लोकेशन
Simple, flowing translated Hindi with Bangla names and places

sections.name: 3.6 प्रश्न-अभ्यास: पाठ के साथ / पाठ के आसपास / भाषा की बात (exercise types)

concepts.text: Why the film took two and a half years; problems faced in specific scenes
Why a dog and the sweet-seller had to be replaced, and how
Why the author calls some events 'luck' in film-making
Activity: write a scene or plan a short film; compare the book and the film
Language: find film-technical words and Bangla-Hindi words; meanings of phrases
Balmukund Gupt (1865-1907), born at Gudiyani, Rohtak (Haryana); journalist of the Bharatendu-Dwivedi period
Edited भारत मित्र and other papers; wrote the satirical essays शिवशंभु के चिट्ठे
A fearless critic of British rule through humorous satire
Lord Curzon was Viceroy of India twice (1899-1905)
The Partition of Bengal (1905) caused great anger among Indians
He resigned after his recommendation for a military post was turned down by the British government
The lesson, from शिवशंभु के चिट्ठे, is written as a farewell address to Curzon
Parting is always sad, even between people who never got along
Animals and birds feel sad at parting; even enemies are moved
Curzon came with pomp (Delhi Durbar 1903) but leaves in humiliation
Ironic question: what did he come for, and what did he do?
His arrogance: he ignored the pleas of millions of Indians against the partition
Nadirshah comparison: even Nadirshah stopped a massacre on one request, but Curzon would not listen to 8 crore people
Indians are reminded of their helplessness under colonial rule
Satire (व्यंग्य) on colonial rulers' arrogance and indifference
Exposure of the British policy of divide and rule
Growth of national feeling and protest through journalism
Letter/speech style (संभाषण) addressed directly to Curzon
Sharp irony, humour and rhetorical questions
Mixed vocabulary: Hindi, Urdu and English words of the period
संभाषण: address/speech; विदाई: farewell; करुणा: pity
वायसराय, दरबार, बंग-भंग: colonial-era terms
नादिरशाह, आसफ़जाह: historical figures in the comparison

sections.name: 4.7 प्रश्न-अभ्यास: पाठ के साथ / पाठ के आसपास / भाषा की बात (exercise types)

concepts.text: Why parting is called sad, and what Curzon gained or lost
Explain the Nadirshah comparison and the Delhi Durbar reference
Why the piece is called satire; quote examples of irony
Discuss the free press and journalism in the freedom movement
Language: find Urdu-English words and idioms; rewrite sentences in simple Hindi
Shekhar Joshi (1932-2022), born in Olia village, Almora (Uttarakhand)
Story collections: कोसी का घटवार, साथ के लोग, हलवाहा, नौरंगी बीमार है; famous story दाज्यू
Writes about hill life, workers and the common man
Mohan, son of the poor priest Vanshidhar, is the brightest student in the village school
Master Trilok Singh makes Mohan class monitor and praises his singing
Dhanram, a blacksmith's son, is weak at studies and is beaten for not learning the table of 13
Dhanram does not envy Mohan and accepts his superiority as natural
Mohan is sent to Lucknow with his relative Ramesh, who treats him as a servant
Mohan studies in an ordinary school, then a technical course, but gets no job
Back in the village, Mohan goes to Dhanram's smithy to get his sickle (हँसुआ) sharpened
Dhanram struggles to shape an iron rod into a round ring
Mohan takes the hammer and shapes it perfectly; Dhanram watches amazed
Mohan sits at the furnace without caste hesitation: the iron melts as caste barriers melt
मोहन: talented, sensitive, humble; a victim of a poor system and selfish relatives
धनराम: hardworking and simple; accepts the caste order but values skill
वंशीधर: poor, devout father with high hopes for his son
रमेश: selfish relative who exploits Mohan
मास्टर त्रिलोक सिंह: strict teacher of the old school of punishment
Caste divisions broken through work and human feeling
Dignity of manual labour and skill
An education system that fails to give jobs; exploitation of village youth
Symbolic title: melting iron = melting of caste pride and false status
Flashback (पूर्वदीप्ति) technique
Hill-region words; simple, realistic language
Symbolism and visual description of the smithy
आफर: smithy; धौंकनी: bellows; हँसुआ: sickle; घन: big hammer
पुरोहित, लोहार: caste-based occupations
Hill words and their meanings

sections.name: 5.7 प्रश्न-अभ्यास: पाठ के साथ / पाठ के आसपास / भाषा की बात (exercise types)

concepts.text: Why Dhanram did not envy Mohan; what Mohan's act at the furnace shows
Explain the title and its symbolism
Compare Mohan's hopes with reality; the role of Ramesh
Discuss caste, education and unemployment today
Language: find regional words and idioms; meaning of key lines
Mannu Bhandari (1931-2021), born at Bhanpura (Madhya Pradesh); writer of the नई कहानी movement
Works: आपका बंटी, महाभोज (novels); यही सच है, एक प्लेट सैलाब, मैं हार गई, त्रिशंकु (stories)
The film रजनीगंधा was based on her story यही सच है; she wrote the TV serial रजनी
Rajni, an aware housewife, visits her neighbour Leela
Leela's son Amit, a good student, gets low marks in maths
The teacher pushes students into private tuition with him; those who refuse get low marks
Rajni meets the headmaster, who is indifferent
She goes to education board officials to fight the tuition racket
She gathers parents and uses the press to build public opinion
A parents' meeting leads the board to make a rule against teachers tutoring their own students
रजनी: bold, sensitive, socially aware woman who cannot bear injustice
लीला: worried, helpless mother
अमित: talented student who suffers because of the system
Rajni's husband: practical and cautious at first, later supportive
Headmaster and officials: an indifferent bureaucracy
Commercialisation of education and the tuition racket
Individual and collective action to reform society
Women's awareness and leadership
Power of the media on public issues
Screenplay (पटकथा) features: scenes, settings, characters' actions, dialogue
Camera and scene directions written in brackets
Difference between a story, a play and a screenplay
ट्यूशन, बोर्ड, हेडमास्टर, अभिभावक, प्रेस: education-system words
पटकथा, दृश्य, संवाद: screenplay terms

sections.name: 6.7 प्रश्न-अभ्यास: पाठ के साथ / पाठ के आसपास / भाषा की बात (exercise types)

concepts.text: Why Rajni took up Amit's case; her steps to fight the system
Role of the headmaster, the board and the press
Discuss tuition culture today and give your view
Activity: turn a story into a short screenplay scene
Language: find English words in Hindi dialogue; spoken-style sentences

chapters.title: आरोह: कृश्न चंदर — जामुन का पेड़

concepts.text: Krishan Chander (1914-1977), born at Wazirabad (now Pakistan); well-known Urdu-Hindi story writer
Works: एक गधे की आत्मकथा, एक वायलिन समुंदर के किनारे, कालू भंगी, अन्नदाता, गद्दार
Known for satire, humour and a progressive outlook
After a storm a jamun tree falls on a man in the Secretariat lawn
Gardener and clerks gather; the clerks recall the tree's tasty jamuns rather than worry about the man
The file moves from department to department: commerce, agriculture, horticulture
Horticulture refuses to cut the tree; the idea of cutting the man out instead (medical/plastic surgery)
Learning the man is a poet, the culture department and the Sahitya Akademi get involved
Foreign affairs: the tree was planted by the Prime Minister of 'Petunia', so cutting it could hurt relations
The order to cut the tree finally comes, but the man is already dead; his 'file' is complete
The trapped man: the helpless common citizen
Clerks and officers: an insensitive bureaucracy
The jamun tree and the file: symbols of red-tapism
Satire on red-tapism (लालफीताशाही) and passing the buck
Rules and files count for more than human life
The system's insensitivity towards the common man
Humorous satire (हास्य-व्यंग्य) built on absurd situations
Office words: फ़ाइल, विभाग, सेक्रेटेरियट, अंडर सेक्रेटरी
Simple Urdu-Hindi mixed language
सेक्रेटेरियट: secretariat; माली: gardener; क्लर्क, सुपरिटेंडेंट, अंडर सेक्रेटरी
हॉर्टीकल्चर, एग्रीकल्चर, कल्चरल विभाग: department names
लालफीताशाही: red-tapism; फ़ाइल चलाना: moving files

sections.name: 7.7 प्रश्न-अभ्यास: पाठ के साथ / पाठ के आसपास / भाषा की बात (exercise types)

concepts.text: How each department passed on the responsibility; the irony of the ending
What the story says about the system; is it still relevant?
Suggest a different ending; write a news report on the incident
Language: find office words, idioms and satirical sentences
Jawaharlal Nehru (1889-1964), born in Allahabad; India's first Prime Minister
Books: हिंदुस्तान की कहानी (Discovery of India), विश्व इतिहास की झलक, मेरी कहानी (autobiography), पिता के पत्र पुत्री के नाम
The lesson is a translated extract from हिंदुस्तान की कहानी
Nehru addressed village meetings (जलसे) during the freedom struggle
People shouted भारत माता की जय; he asked them who Bharat Mata is
Farmers answered that it was the earth/land (धरती)
Nehru explained: mountains, rivers, forests and fields are part of it, but above all its crores of people
You yourselves are Bharat Mata: the people's eyes lit up at this new idea
Farmers knew India through pilgrimages and travel; their problems of poverty and debt
The nation as its people, not just its land
Unity in diversity of India
Building national feeling among villagers
Nehru's method: asking questions and building on the people's answers
Freedom means freedom and well-being for these crores of people
Reflective, explanatory prose in translated Hindi
Simple dialogue with the people
जलसा: public meeting; नारा: slogan
धरती, पर्वत, नदियाँ, जंगल, खेत: parts of the idea of the nation
किसान, ज़मींदार, कर्ज़: words for rural life and its problems
Tatsam words such as राष्ट्र, एकता, विविधता and their use

sections.name: 8.6 प्रश्न-अभ्यास: पाठ के साथ / पाठ के आसपास / भाषा की बात (exercise types)

concepts.text: Who Bharat Mata is in Nehru's view; how he explained it to farmers
Explain the lines about mountains, rivers and people
Discuss what the nation means to you
Language: tatsam words and their meanings; sentence transformation

chapters.title: आरोह: कबीर — हम तौ एक एक करि जांनां; संतो देखत जग बौराना

concepts.text: Kabir (c.1398-1518), saint-poet of Kashi; raised by the weaver couple Niru and Nima
Leading poet of निर्गुण भक्ति, ज्ञानाश्रयी शाखा
Works collected in बीजक: साखी, सबद, रमैनी
Language: सधुक्कड़ी / पंचमेल खिचड़ी (a mix of many dialects)

sections.name: 9.2 पद 1: हम तौ एक एक करि जांनां

concepts.text: Kabir believes God is one; those who see two fall into hell (दोजग)
The same air, water and light are in all beings
Example of the potter: many pots from the same clay
Example of the carpenter: he cuts wood but cannot cut the fire within it
God lives in every heart; Kabir is fearless, having found the whole truth
The world has gone mad: it beats those who speak the truth and believes lies
Criticism of ritual-bound Hindus and Muslims (नेमी, धरमी, pir-auliya, idol worship)
Mockery of the show of tilak, caps, beads and false gurus
Hindus love Ram, Muslims love Rahim; they fight and die without knowing the truth
Oneness of God and of humanity
Critique of outward ritual, hypocrisy and religious division
Self-knowledge and inner devotion
Devices: दृष्टांत (potter and clay), अनुप्रास, रूपक
Pad form, singable (गेयता); direct, fearless tone
Simple folk vocabulary with Persian-Arabic words
शांत रस dominant; rebellious, satirical tone (व्यंग्य)
Direct address 'संतो' and questions to engage listeners
जांनां: knew; दोजग: hell; कुम्हार: potter; बौराना: to go mad
नेमी-धरमी: ritual-bound people; पीर-औलिया: Muslim saints; टोपी, माला, तिलक: outward symbols
Common sadhukkadi forms and their standard Hindi meanings

sections.name: 9.7 प्रश्न-अभ्यास: कविता के साथ / कविता के आसपास (exercise types)

concepts.text: Explain how Kabir shows that God is one
Explain the 'madness' of the world and the examples of hypocrisy
सप्रसंग व्याख्या of given lines; identify devices
Compare Kabir's views with other bhakti poets

chapters.title: आरोह: मीरा — मेरे तो गिरधर गोपाल; पग घुँघरू बाँधि

concepts.text: Mirabai (c.1498-1546), born at Kudki, Merta (Rajasthan); married into the Mewar royal family
Krishna devotee; सगुण भक्ति with माधुर्य भाव
Language: Rajasthani mixed with Braj and Gujarati; pads collected in पदावली

sections.name: 10.2 पद 1: मेरे तो गिरधर गोपाल, दूसरो न कोई

concepts.text: Krishna, wearing a peacock crown, is her only husband
She gave up family honour (कुल की कानि) and sat among saints
She watered the vine of love with her tears (प्रेम-बेलि)
Churning image: she took the butter (devotion) and left the buttermilk (the world)
Devotees make her happy, the world makes her weep; she prays to be saved

sections.name: 10.3 पद 2: पग घुँघरू बाँधि मीरां नाची

concepts.text: Mira dances with bells on her feet before Krishna
People call her mad (बावरी) and a disgrace to the family
The Rana sends poison; she drinks it laughing
She finds the eternal Lord with ease
Complete devotion and surrender to Krishna
Defiance of social and family limits placed on women
Pain and joy of love (विरह, समर्पण)
Autobiographical touch: her own life events appear in the pads
Devices: रूपक (प्रेम-बेलि), पुनरुक्ति प्रकाश (सींचि-सींचि), अनुप्रास
Singable pad form; emotional, simple language
भक्ति रस with माधुर्य (श्रृंगार) bhav
गिरधर गोपाल: Krishna who lifted the mountain; मोर मुकुट: peacock crown
कुल की कानि: family honour; लोक-लाज: public shame; बावरी: crazy
दधि, घृत, छोई: curd, ghee, buttermilk residue
राणा, विष का प्याला, अविनासी: words from the poison episode

sections.name: 10.7 प्रश्न-अभ्यास: कविता के साथ / कविता के आसपास (exercise types)

concepts.text: How Mira describes her devotion and what she gave up
Explain the churning image and the poison episode
सप्रसंग व्याख्या; identify devices
Compare Mira's devotion with Kabir's

chapters.title: आरोह: भवानी प्रसाद मिश्र — घर की याद

concepts.text: Bhawani Prasad Mishra (1913-1985), born at Tigaria, Hoshangabad (MP); Gandhian poet
Jailed during the Quit India Movement (1942)
Works: गीतफ़रोश, चकित है दुख, अँधेरी कविताएँ, बुनी हुई रस्सी (Sahitya Akademi)
In jail on a rainy night, the poet remembers home
He recalls four brothers, four sisters, his mother and father
Father: strong, cheerful and energetic though old; reads the Gita, laughs loudly
Mother: simple, unlettered, full of love
Rain makes him picture the scene at home: siblings, mother weeping, father acting strong
Contrast between his lonely cell and the lively home
He asks the monsoon (सावन) to carry a message: tell them he is happy and well
He asks it not to tell them of his pain
Love for family and the pain of separation
Sacrifice for the nation versus personal feelings
Patriotism: the poet chose jail for the nation
Indian family bonds and the father's role
Personification of the monsoon (मानवीकरण): सावन as messenger
Conversational tone, simple language, repetition
Imagery of home and rain
सावन: rainy month; झड़ी: steady rain; संदेशा: message
Family words: भाई-बहन, पिता, माँ, घर-आँगन
Words showing the father's nature: भारी-भरकम, खुशमिज़ाज, दौड़-धूप

sections.name: 11.6 प्रश्न-अभ्यास: कविता के साथ / कविता के आसपास (exercise types)

concepts.text: Describe the father's personality as shown in the poem
Why the poet asks the monsoon to hide his pain
सप्रसंग व्याख्या; identify devices
Write about a family member you miss

chapters.title: आरोह: त्रिलोचन — चंपा काले काले अच्छर नहीं चीन्हती

concepts.text: Trilochan (1917-2007), born at Kathghara Chirani Patti, Sultanpur (UP); progressive (प्रगतिशील) poet
Works: धरती, गुलाब और बुलबुल, दिगंत, ताप के ताए हुए दिन (Sahitya Akademi)
Known for writing sonnets in Hindi
Champa, daughter of the cowherd Sundar, cannot read
She wonders how sounds come out of black letters
She is playful and hides the poet's pen and papers
The poet asks her to learn to read; she refuses
He says that after marriage her husband may go to Calcutta and she will need to write letters
Champa says she won't let him go and curses Calcutta (कलकत्ते पर बजर गिरे)
Importance of literacy
Migration (पलायन) from villages to cities and separation of families
Innocence and wisdom of a rural girl
Contrast between the educated poet and the unlettered but sharp Champa
Champa's attitude reflects women's fear of loneliness in migrant families
Narrative and dialogue style; free verse
Folk vocabulary (अच्छर, चीन्हती, बजर)
अच्छर: letters; चीन्हना: to recognise; बजर गिरे: may thunder strike (a curse)
चरवाहा: cowherd; गाय-भैंस, चरवाही: pastoral words
Awadhi-flavoured words and their standard Hindi forms

sections.name: 12.6 प्रश्न-अभ्यास: कविता के साथ / कविता के आसपास (exercise types)

concepts.text: Why Champa refuses to read; what she thinks of Calcutta
Explain the poet's argument for education
Discuss migration; write a letter in Champa's voice
सप्रसंग व्याख्या of lines; meanings of folk words
Dushyant Kumar (1933-1975), born at Rajpur Nawada, Bijnor (UP); made the ghazal popular in Hindi
Works: साये में धूप (ghazals), सूर्य का स्वागत, आवाज़ों के घेरे, एक कंठ विषपायी
A lamp was promised for every home, but now there is not one even for the city
Shade of trees feels like sun: institutions meant to give relief hurt people
Poor people without clothes cover themselves with their knees
Rulers are sure the stone (the system) cannot melt; the poet wants power in his voice
Rulers may silence poets; the poet will still speak
Live under one's own gulmohar, die for gulmohar in others' lanes: living and dying with dignity
Ghazal: a series of sher (couplets), each complete in itself
Terms: मतला (first sher), मक़ता (last sher with the pen-name), रदीफ़, क़ाफ़िया, बहर
Disillusionment after independence; broken political promises
Poverty and suppression of voices; hope for change
Symbols: चिराग, दरख्त, साये में धूप, गुलमोहर
Hindi-Urdu blended language; irony
चिराग़ाँ: lamps; मयस्सर: available; दरख़्त: tree; साये: shade
मुतमइन: assured; बेक़रार: restless; निज़ाम: rule/system; एहतियात: caution
बहर: metre; गुलमोहर: flame tree, a symbol of beauty and dignity

sections.name: 13.7 प्रश्न-अभ्यास: कविता के साथ / कविता के आसपास (exercise types)

concepts.text: Explain the symbolism of the lamp, the shade and the gulmohar
Explain each sher; identify radif and kafiya
Discuss what the poet says about the system
Discuss how the ghazal reflects the political mood of the 1970s

chapters.title: आरोह: अक्क महादेवी — हे भूख! मत मचल; हे मेरे जूही के फूल जैसे ईश्वर

concepts.text: Akka Mahadevi (12th century), born at Udutadi near Shimoga (Karnataka)
Devotee of Shiva (चन्नमल्लिकार्जुन); part of the Veerashaiva movement led by Basavanna
Wrote वचन in Kannada; translated into Hindi by Kedarnath Singh
Addresses hunger, thirst, sleep and other urges, asking them to calm down
Asks greed, anger, attachment, pride and jealousy to leave her
Control of the senses for devotion to Shiva

sections.name: 14.3 वचन 2: हे मेरे जूही के फूल जैसे ईश्वर

concepts.text: Asks God to make her beg and give up all possessions
Asks that even begged food fall before it reaches her mouth, or a dog snatch it
Total surrender and the end of ego
Renunciation and control over desires
Devotion through self-surrender
The poet's journey from royal life to the life of an ascetic
Link to the spread of the Bhakti movement across India
Address form (संबोधन); personification of hunger and urges
उपमा: God like a jasmine flower
Vachana: short devotional prose-poetry
मचलना: to be restless; मद: pride; मत्सर: jealousy; मोह: attachment
चन्नमल्लिकार्जुन: Shiva, Akka's beloved Lord
जूही: jasmine; भीख, झोली: begging words

sections.name: 14.7 प्रश्न-अभ्यास: कविता के साथ / कविता के आसपास (exercise types)

concepts.text: Why the poet addresses hunger and the other urges
Why she wishes for poverty; meaning of losing the ego
सप्रसंग व्याख्या; identify devices

chapters.title: आरोह: अवतार सिंह पाश — सबसे खतरनाक

concepts.text: Pash (Avtar Singh Sandhu, 1950-1988), born at Talwandi Salem, Jalandhar (Punjab); revolutionary Punjabi poet
Works: लौहकथा, उड्डदे बाजां मगर, साडे समियां विच; Hindi translations such as बीच का रास्ता नहीं होता
Killed by terrorists in 1988
Robbery of labour, police beatings and greed are bad, but not the most dangerous
Most dangerous: being filled with deathly calm (मुर्दा शांति) and losing all restlessness
Bearing everything silently; a routine of home to work and back
A watch that runs on the wrist but seems stopped in one's eyes
Eyes that see everything but feel nothing; songs that turn into sighs
The moon rising over a scene of murder no longer hurts
Contrast between evils that harm the body and those that kill the spirit
Most dangerous of all: the death of our dreams
Warning against complacency and loss of feeling
A revolutionary call to keep dreams and resistance alive
Free verse; repetition of 'सबसे खतरनाक'
Symbols and images: घड़ी, आँख, चाँद, गीत
Contrast between ordinary evils and the deeper danger
मुर्दा शांति: deathly calm; तड़प: restless longing
लोभ, गद्दारी, पुलिस की मार: the lesser evils listed
सपनों का मर जाना: death of dreams (the central phrase)

sections.name: 15.6 प्रश्न-अभ्यास: कविता के साथ / कविता के आसपास (exercise types)

concepts.text: Explain what the poet calls most dangerous, and why
Explain the images of the watch, the eye and the moon
Discuss: is the poem relevant today?
सप्रसंग व्याख्या; identify devices

chapters.title: आरोह: निर्मला पुतुल — आओ, मिलकर बचाएँ

concepts.text: Nirmala Putul (b. 1972), born at Dudhani Kurwa, Dumka (Jharkhand); Santhali poet
Works: नगाड़े की तरह बजते शब्द, अपने घर की तलाश में
The poem is translated from Santhali into Hindi (by Ashok Singh)
A call to save the Santhal Pargana from the influence of city culture
Save the land, language, songs, simplicity and pride in dark skin
Save the forests, mountains, rivers and the smell of the earth
Save the warrior spirit: the bowstring, the sharp arrow, the axe-edge
Save trust, hope and open laughter; much is still left to save
Fear of losing identity through outside (urban) contact
Keep the inner fire and courage alive
Tribal identity and culture under threat
Protecting the environment; resisting displacement and consumerism
Free verse; imagery of tribal life
Repetition (बचाएँ) as an appeal; local words
संथाल परगना: tribal region of Jharkhand
झारखंडीपन: Jharkhandi identity; भोलापन: innocence
धनुष की डोरी, तीर, कुल्हाड़ी: tools showing tribal strength
Santhali cultural words: songs, dance, forest produce

sections.name: 16.6 प्रश्न-अभ्यास: कविता के साथ / कविता के आसपास (exercise types)

concepts.text: What the poet wants to save, and why
Explain the meaning of झारखंडीपन
Discuss threats to tribal life; write an appeal
सप्रसंग व्याख्या; identify devices

chapters.title: वितान: कुमार गंधर्व — भारतीय गायिकाओं में बेजोड़: लता मंगेशकर

concepts.text: Kumar Gandharva (1924-1992), born near Belgaum (Karnataka); Hindustani classical singer
Known for nirguni bhajans of Kabir; Padma Vibhushan
The author first heard Lata Mangeshkar on the radio and was charmed
Lata's singing has true 'गानपन' (musicality), clarity and sweetness
Comparison with Noorjahan; Lata's voice is purer
Film music made common people musically aware
Lata's singing raised the taste of ordinary listeners
Film music and classical music compared; both have value
A three-minute song can match a three-hour concert in emotional effect
Good film music must touch the listener's heart in a short time
Author's view: Lata's karuna (sad) songs are less effective; she sings at a high pitch
Film music's use of folk music
The author defends film music against classical purists
Lata as an unmatched singer
Classical vs light music; the importance of rasa and musical sense
Music terms: स्वर, लय, ताल, गानपन, रंजकता, शास्त्रीय संगीत
Critical yet admiring style
गानपन: the essence of musicality
सुरीलापन, नादमय उच्चार, कोमलता, मुग्धता: qualities of Lata's voice
चित्रपट संगीत vs शास्त्रीय संगीत; ताल, लय, आलाप
What गानपन is; why Lata is called unique
Compare classical and film music
Explain the author's criticism of Lata's karuna songs
Discuss: can film music be called art?
Activity: listen to songs and discuss them

chapters.title: वितान: अनुपम मिश्र — राजस्थान की रजत बूँदें

concepts.text: Anupam Mishra (1948-2016), born in Wardha (Maharashtra); Gandhian environmentalist
Works: आज भी खरे हैं तालाब, राजस्थान की रजत बूँदें
Kui (कुंई): a narrow, deep well in the Rajasthan desert
A kui collects रेजाणीपानी: moisture held in the sand above a gypsum (खड़िया) layer
Kui vs ordinary well: depth, diameter and source of water
Chejaros (expert diggers) dig kuis; workers above throw sand down to send in fresh air
Kui walls are lined with rope of खींप grass
Three forms of water: पालरपानी (surface rainwater), पातालपानी (groundwater), रेजाणीपानी
Kui water is sweet while well water is often salty
Chejaros once got gifts and respect; now they get only wages
Kuis are private but stand on community land, controlled by the village society
Areas: Churu, Bikaner, Jaisalmer, Barmer
Traditional water harvesting and community wisdom
Importance of saving water
Respect for skilled workers in traditional society
Water as a shared resource controlled by the community
Lessons for today's water crisis and other states' efforts
कुंई: small, deep desert well; चेजारो: skilled kui-maker
खड़िया पट्टी: gypsum layer; खींप: desert grass for rope
रेजाणीपानी, पालरपानी, पातालपानी: the three forms of water
मरुभूमि, रेत, नमी, खारा पानी: desert words
What a kui is and how it differs from a well
How the chapter helps with the water crisis
How society's treatment of chejaros has changed
Why the community controls privately owned kuis
Explain पालरपानी, पातालपानी, रेजाणीपानी
Baby Halder, a domestic worker whose autobiography आलो-आँधारि was written in Bangla
Translated into Hindi by Prabodh Kumar, her employer 'Tatush'
Separated from her husband, she lives with her three children and looks for a house and work
She faces trouble with landlords, and her house is demolished
She works in Tatush's home; he encourages her to read and write
Tatush gives her notebooks and a pen; she starts writing in Bangla
Tatush's friends read her writing and encourage her
Neighbours gossip about a woman living alone
Her elder son works away from home; she worries about him
Her life story is published; she gains dignity and a new identity as a writer
Women's struggle and self-respect
Writing as empowerment
Tatush's kindness
Exploitation and insecurity of domestic workers
Society's suspicion of a woman living without her husband
आलो-आँधारि: light and darkness (Bangla)
तातुश: affectionate name for her employer
घरेलू काम, किराया, मकान मालिक: words of her daily struggle
आत्मकथा: the autobiography genre
How Tatush helped Baby Halder
Society's view of single women
What reading and writing meant to her
Discuss the meaning of the title
Write about the life of a domestic worker you know
